correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the draw gives X'=X+alpha eta with E[eta|X,T]=X/T and eta squared equal to 1. The second-moment map is affine with slope 1+2 alpha/T. Applying the two maps at totals T and T+c gives PF minus FP equal to 2c(c-d)(V/T+d)/(T+c), where V is the preceding uncentered second moment. For d=a-b>0 this is strictly positive, and the common suffix has positive slopes. Adjacent exchanges give both unique sorted endpoints for arbitrary horizons and budgets. The Pólya continuation formula follows either from the conditional beta law or from the invariant (V+cT)/(4T(T+c)) under one more P step and bounded convergence of the Pólya fraction martingale. At d=0 a balanced initial state gives a two-step tie; for d<0 the swap sign depends on V/T+d. Already for two steps, balance gives a negative sign and sufficiently imbalanced positive starting counts give a positive sign for any d<0. For the explicit (a,b)=(1,3) examples the differences are -48/7 and 528/35. The theorem optimizes uncentered squared imbalance under precommitted schedules, not variance or adaptive policies.
